correctness.rationale: Deriving the unique temperature solution on three subintervals and integrating its square gives the exact derivative rho(1-b)P(q)/q², with q=e^{-s}. For nonnegative initial loads P(C)>0. If m≥1 it is positive everywhere; if m<1 strict concavity gives precisely one possible sign change in the admissible q interval, with P(1) determined by m-mcrit. This establishes global uniqueness and the sharp boundary. At q=sqrt(C), P>0 proves the optimizer precedes the midpoint. The larger cubic root has negative derivative, so parameter derivatives have their claimed signs. The implicit function theorem after rescaling q=sqrt(C)z gives the stated O(exp(-(H-d)/2)) asymptotic. Symbolic identity check gave zero discrepancy and embedded standard-library checker gave 51,592 additional finite numerical assertions. Those tests are not used as proofs of infinitary statements.

value.rationale: Timed shading with a fixed duration and depth is experimentally meaningful because the total solar reduction is fixed. The exact initial thermal-state threshold separates immediate treatment from a unique interior placement, and stronger treatment versus larger antecedent heat act in opposing monotone directions. The strict early placement and long-day leading shift independent of shade strength offer an analytic baseline for thermal-inertia sensitivity studies rather than a routine point computation. No empirical agronomic benefit or calibrated crop-yield optimum is asserted.
